outline.note: Fade in low on the reactor building; the camera rises into the hero view. Then the presenters, the title, the QR.
The camera rises; the plant shrinks into a point while Lithuania opens around it: wind turns, solar shines, power flows to the cities. "50 %" counts up once.
A calm night: the turbines slow, the sun sets, local flows fade, imports grow; a controllable node lights up. "And when there is no wind or sun?"
Lithuania warms up: the country is assessing the BWRX-300 (memorandum, February 2026).
Down into the node: the plant grows back out of it as the map closes; beside it a generic ~1,500 MW unit rises. Labels ~1,500 MW / ~300 MW.
Four more BWRX-300 units assemble one after another behind ours: 5 × 300 MW. The large unit steps back.
The comparison falls away; our plant remains. "~300 MW" counts up once.
Two football pitches are drawn beside the power block at true scale.
"24-36 months*" with its qualifier: vendor estimate, first nuclear concrete to fuel load, series unit.
Up into geography: the plant becomes the Darlington pin as the North Atlantic opens; the other pins appear one by one, styled by status.
The camera glides to Canada: Darlington, under construction (CNSC licence April 2025); the other pins step back.
Into the Darlington pin: the plant grows out of it as the map closes, landing on the approved hero view (no title card).
The approved Stage 3 descent, replayed: ground, shaft, containment; the vessel opens on the core (master 0-15.4 s).
From a spot on the fuel the micro view opens: neutron → U-235 → split → heat → new neutrons → a second complete split. Loops calmly.
The micro view closes into the fuel spot as warmth: this happens inside these fuel bundles.
From the warm spot back out: the fuel, the bundles, then the control blades in plan, copper; the reaction cue (glints) at full.
One key: the blades move in; the glints thin out.
Another key: the blades move back out; the glints return.
The control demo settles; water rises through the core and boils; the mixture rises through the chimney; cooler water returns down the sides.
Separators throw the water out, the dryer catches the last drops: dry steam leaves the vessel.
Steam runs along the main steam line to the turbine; the shaft starts turning.
Under the turbine the condenser turns exhaust steam back into water; pumps send it back to the reactor. The water cycle closes.
The generator sends electricity out of the hall, through the transformer, along the line: the city lights up (scale illustration).
Back from the city to the plant, still running: reactor, pools, turbine hall, the line to the grid. Nothing is reset.
External power is lost: the line goes dark, the hall lights go out, the site dims, steam stops, the turbine winds down.
The chain reaction stops: every blade goes in, the glints die out.
But the heat does not go away: the vessel stays warm (decay heat). Fission ≈ 0, heat ≠ 0.
The isolation condenser loop: steam rises to the submerged condensers, heat goes into the pool, water returns by gravity. No pump.
Time runs once: 0 h → 1 day → … → 7 days, then stops; the passive loop keeps running.
The rhythm slows: wide over the plant; three restrained words appear around it, one after another.
Reverse journey: vessel, containment, shaft and ground close as the camera rises out; the grid reconnects; back to the opening composition.
The opening composition again: one closing line, the presenters, e-mails, QR, "Your questions". Holds for Q&A.
